podcast.title: 1995 Bankruptcy
podcast.body: Despite having two multi-platinum albums, the trio declared bankruptcy in 1995 because they were only netting a few thousand dollars per year each. This move was made to renegotiate their contract with LaFace Records and their manager, Pebbles. "So TLC declared bankruptcy in 1995 in order to renegotiate their contract with label LaFace Records and manager Pebbles."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Grammy Nomination (1997)
podcast.body: TLC was among the artists whose multi-platinum albums in the mid-90s represented the contemporary sound of the era, but did not win Album of the Year. "Dion's competition that year included the aforementioned Otolay by Beck, the Fuji's seminal hip-hop smash The Score. Smashing Pumpkins' Magnum Opus, Melon Colley and the Infinite Sadness. And the acclaimed babyface produced soundtrack to Waiting to Exhale. All of these were multi-platinum albums, yes, even Beck's. And all of them sounded more like the mid-90s than Selene Dion's album did."

podcast.title: 1999 Singles Chart Dominance
podcast.body: TLC was a prominent act on the singles charts in 1999, reflecting their continued success and influence in popular music. "Meanwhile, the singles charts were dominated by Cher, TLC, Christina Aguilar, Ricky Martin, Art Kelly, and Destiny's Child."

podcast.body: TLC, identified as a "Multi-platinum R&B trio," was among the artists competing against Santana in the major Grammy categories at the 42nd annual awards in 2000. "Multi-platinum R&B trio TLC."

podcast.title: Lisa "Left Eye" Lopez's Death (2002)
podcast.body: Three years after their last major hit "Unpretty," Lisa "Left Eye" Lopez tragically died at 30 years old in a car crash in Honduras while filming a documentary. "Three years later, Lisa left-eye Lopez, died in a car crash while filming a documentary in Honduras. She was 30 years old."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: "Blueprint for Female Ensembles"
podcast.body: Critics later recognized TLC as "the blueprint for female ensembles to follow," indicating their significant influence on subsequent girl groups. "Critics would later call TLC, quote, the blueprint for female ensembles to follow."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: "No Scrubs" Cover on Teal Album
podcast.body: TLC's song "No Scrubs" was covered on Weezer's Teal Album, marking the only exception to the album's rule of covering songs released before 1994, because the band simply thought it was "cool." "TLC's No Scrups. It made the cut because the band decided that it was, well, it was just cool."

podcast.title: Blanked at Major Categories (General)
podcast.body: TLC was listed among other rap/hip-hop artists who have been "blanked" in major general field Grammy categories, despite their commercial success and critical acclaim. "In addition to B, J, Kanye and Kendrick, major category nominees that have been blanked include MC Hammer, Coolio, TLC, Nelly, Eminem, Ludicrous, Lil Wayne and Missy Elliott."

podcast.title: Formation and Nicknames
podcast.body: The trio was formed by producer Pebbles, who introduced Tion Watkins and Lisa Lopez (from Atlanta) and suggested replacing their third member with Rozonda Thomas. Pebbles named the group TLC and helped the women pick their iconic nicknames: Tion Watkins became T-Boz, Lisa Lopez became Left Eye, and Rozonda Thomas became Chilli. "Pebbles named the trio TLC and helped the women pick nicknames to form the acronym. Watkins became T-Baws, Lopez became Left Eye and Thomas became Chile, TLC."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Hip Hop Integration
podcast.body: TLC's edge in the girl group scene was their tight relationship to hip hop, with Left Eye specifically contributing "serious rap bars" on most of their hits. This set them apart from other R&B groups. "What gave TLC an edge in the girl group sweepstakes was their even tighter relationship to hip hop. Left Eye threw down serious rap bars on most of their hits."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: LaFace Records' Flagship Girl Group
podcast.body: TLC was the flagship girl group for LaFace Records in the mid-1990s, when the label was riding high with successful R&B acts. Their sound, particularly on hits like "No Scrubs," influenced the direction the label initially pursued for Pink's debut. "L.A. Reed and his team felt Pink could play both sides of the fence, not unlike their flagship girl group TLC."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Second Biggest Girl Group in Chart History
podcast.body: Billboard ranks TLC as the second biggest girl group in chart history, positioned behind The Supremes and ahead of Destiny's Child. "Billboard ranks the pointer sisters as the fourth biggest girl group in chart history, after in third place Destiny's Child, in second place TLC..."

podcast.title: Three-Year Hiatus and Side Projects
podcast.body: After the 1995 bankruptcy, the group entered a tumultuous three-year hiatus during which Left Eye and T-Boz both worked on side projects that almost became permanent. They were eventually persuaded to reunite for their third album, "FanMail." "After a tumultuous three-year hiatus during which both Left Eye and T-Boss worked on side projects that almost became permanent, the trio were persuaded to reunite for a third album."
